promptState.text: Describe this image as one detailed caption that would recreate it as closely as possible. Describe only what you see, and never mention the image or an original. If a change is written below, write the caption with that change.
Make it a snowy winter scene: the bunny stands in soft snow and wears a red knitted scarf.

aiPromptState.formula:
You are the prompt upsampler of a text-to-image model. Expand the user's short request into ONE detailed, self-contained caption: the exact text the image model receives. Output only the caption, with no greetings, explanations, refusals, questions, Markdown, headings, JSON, coordinates, ids or angle-bracket tokens, and no quotes around it. If the input is not clearly an image request, caption a visualization of its concept. The request may begin with a "TARGET CANVAS: W:H" line: compose for that canvas (wide spreads content sideways, tall stacks it) and never mention the ratio or the canvas.

Fidelity and planning: keep every explicit subject, attribute, count, spatial constraint, style cue and piece of wording; never contradict, substitute, drop or narrow the request, and keep an abstract concept abstract. Decide everything left open as ONE concrete, consistent plan; never offer alternatives or hedge. Never re-express a stated constraint through another mechanism; add camera optics (depth of field, bokeh, blur) only when asked for or implied. Without a stated style, plan an actual photograph and open with the medium convention ("Full-color outdoor photograph, ...", "Full-color indoor photograph, ...", "Studio photograph, ...", "Close-up photograph, ..."); keep "Photorealistic" for renders, and turn "photorealistic" or "realistic" requests for photos into the photograph convention. Give a photograph a few ordinary, non-ideal specifics drawn from the scene's own objects instead of the stock-photo ideal. Do not invent names, brands, logos or celebrities; keep user-named ones. A long request keeps its content but not its wording: drop appraisal and sales vocabulary, turn moods into observable physical facts, and add only new concrete content with positions. Time of day is lighting, not rendered text.

Caption format: one continuous prose block in the generative voice, never "this image shows", "we can see" or "is visible". Lead with medium and style, then scene, lighting and camera, then the subjects with concrete colors, materials and state. Every person in focus gets an observable profile: ethnicity, gender, age range, skin tone ("fair skin", "brown skin"), hair and clothing. Make the layout reconstructable from words: frame-relative positions (frame-left, frame-right, upper, lower, foreground, midground, background), sentence-initial anchors ("On the left, ...", "In the background, ..."), relations (holds, faces, behind) and a consistent order; describe up to about ten instances one by one, beyond that give the exact count and arrangement. Out-of-focus or distant planes are shapes, colors and silhouettes, never identities or readable text, and the background takes about a sixth of the caption. Be definite: no hedging adverbs, no quality or emotion judgments, no closing sentence about mood; state negations as what is present. Rendered text: transcribe every wording verbatim inside double quotes in its original language and script, keep the line breaks of multi-line text, and give its typography, color and placement; author concrete, domain-correct wording when the request needs text it does not supply, and name canonical structures (calendar, keyboard, periodic table) exactly with their full layout. All prose is English; only quoted text keeps its language. Typical length is 100 to 350 words, more for complex scenes.

Output only the caption.

{"version":1,"content":"

MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 FLUX 3 needs ComfyUI 0.41.0 or newer, the first version with FLUX 3. On an older ComfyUI, Load CLIP has no flux3 type and some nodes show red: update ComfyUI first.

 FLUX 3 needs a free approval first (one time only)

Black Forest Labs keeps the FLUX 3 files behind a short approval on Hugging Face. Until you do it, every FLUX 3 download link below answers "Access to model ... is restricted ... Please log in".

  1. Log in to Hugging Face (a free account).
  2. Open the FLUX 3 model page with the button below and click Agree and access repository. Access is given at once.
  3. Now the download links below work, in the same browser.

FLUX 3 Klein on Hugging Face 

 Downloading with ComfyUI-Manager or a script needs a Hugging Face token as well (hf auth login). In the browser, being logged in is enough.

 Load Diffusion Model

Download flux3-image-klein-int8-convrot.safetensors5.83 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/flux3

Create the flux3 folder if it does not exist.

Take the file WITHOUT base in its name: that is the distilled (fast) model these workflows use. The files with base in the name are the base model, made for training LoRAs: it needs CFG 3.5 and 25 to 50 steps, and at the settings here (15 or 16 steps, CFG 1) its pictures come out smeared and broken.

Already have flux3_image_klein_sd_int8_convrot.safetensors? That is the same file under its first name (ComfyUI's own template used it at launch). Pick it in this node instead of downloading it again.

 Load CLIP

Download qwen3vl_4b_int8_convrot.safetensors4.86 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

 Load VAE

Download flux2-vae.safetensors336 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

The same file as Flux 2 Klein: if you have it, skip this one.

 License

FLUX 3 Image Klein is released under the FLUX Kommunity License. You may use the pictures commercially only while your yearly revenue (all the money coming in, before costs), together with any company you belong to, is under US$5 million. Read it before you use the model for paid work.

FLUX 3 Klein model page 

 Load CLIP (the prompt upsampler)

Download qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_w4a8.safetensors6.72 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

The same file as workflow 3. The bigger int8_convrot one (9.75 GB) works too.

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using the R shortcut.

 Nodes Installed from Manager

  • Pixaroma: update to the latest version (these workflows need at least 1.4.218). A node shows red or missing? Update Pixaroma.

Which version is the newest? The Latest Pixaroma version button shows it and what is new in it. The help page has the update steps for every kind of install.

Latest Pixaroma version How to update Pixaroma 

 Something missing?

Each button opens a short video that shows the fix, with the steps written under it.

Red or missing nodes A model file is missing Buttons missing after an update 

 Resources

Join Discord  Pixaroma YouTube Channel  Ask for help

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Give it a picture: the AI looks at it and writes a detailed prompt that describes it, and FLUX 3 draws a new picture from that prompt. Turn the Switch to + my extra instructions and the AI writes the prompt with your change in it: the same character in the snow, in a forest, in other clothes.

 Steps

  1. Load your picture in Load Image Mini Pixaroma.
  2. Pick a size close to your picture's shape on Sizes Pixaroma.
  3. Leave the picture seed on F to repeat, or switch it to R for a new picture from the same written prompt.
  4. Write your change in extra instructions (step 4).
  5. On Switch Pixaroma, click as it is for a copy, or + my extra instructions for a copy with your change.
  6. Press Run. Read the prompt the AI wrote in Show Text Pixaroma.

 Writing extra instructions

  • One or two sentences about what changes: Make it a snowy winter scene: the bunny stands in soft snow and wears a red knitted scarf.
  • Say only the change. The AI keeps everything else from your picture.
  • The prompt above it (the copy instruction) is tested wording: leave it as it is.

 Two seeds

  • AI Prompt Pixaroma has its own seed for the written prompt (F / R on the node). On F it keeps the prompt it wrote until you change the picture or the words; press Re-roll on it for a different prompt.
  • Seed Pixaroma is the picture's seed. Change it for a new picture from the same prompt: the AI does not run again, so it is quick.

 Good to know

  • It is not an exact copy. FLUX 3 draws the picture again from words: the same character, clothes, pose and background, but colours, proportions and small details shift. In our tests the bunny's olive green clothes came out a little darker and its fur more detailed.
  • For the SAME picture with a change, use the Image Edit workflows: they keep your picture and change only what you ask.
  • It needs about 6.7 GB more memory, and the first Run loads the upsampler.
  • A Run stops with a CUDA error such as illegal memory access while the AI writes (seen on RTX 30 cards)? Restart ComfyUI, open the gear on AI Prompt Pixaroma and turn off Faster writing (MTP) under Behaviour (Pixaroma 1.4.223 or newer). The prompt then comes out a little different and takes a few seconds longer.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

What AI Prompt needs Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (FLUX 3 Klein, distilled) - The image model, FLUX 3 Image Klein from Black Forest Labs, the distilled version (no base in the file name): 15 steps, CFG 1. It makes a picture from words AND changes a picture you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 4B, reads the prompt) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something FLUX 3 understands. The type must be flux3.
  • Load VAE (Flux 2 VAE) - Turns the finished render into a picture. FLUX 3 uses the same VAE as Flux 2.
  • Load CLIP (the prompt upsampler, Qwen 3.5 9B) - The prompt upsampler: a small language model from Black Forest Labs that can also SEE pictures. Here it looks at your picture and writes the long, detailed prompt FLUX 3 was trained on. The smaller w4a8 file (6.7 GB).

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (1. your picture) - The picture to copy. Click it to upload your own, or pick one from the list. Tested with a photo of a room and a 3D character.
  • Sizes Pixaroma (2. picture size) - The size of the new picture. Pick the shape closest to your picture's: the demo picture is square, so 1024 x 1024. The Portrait / Landscape switch turns a size on its side.
  • Seed Pixaroma (3. picture seed) - The seed for the PICTURE. F (fixed) repeats it, R (random) gives a new picture from the same written prompt every Run. The written prompt has its own seed, on AI Prompt Pixaroma. The demo uses seed 3.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (the copy instruction, leave it) - Tells the AI to describe your picture so FLUX 3 can draw it again. Tested wording: leave it as it is.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (4. extra instructions) - Your change, in a sentence or two: a new place, a season, a piece of clothing. It is added after the copy instruction, and only used when the Switch is on + my extra instructions.
  • Switch Pixaroma (5. as it is, or with extra instructions) - Click a row: as it is copies your picture, + my extra instructions copies it with your change.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • AI Prompt Pixaroma (looks at the picture, writes the prompt) - Runs the upsampler with Black Forest Labs' own instructions (the preset FLUX 3 - prompt from an idea), sent as a system message. It looks at your picture and reads the instruction from Switch Pixaroma. Its own seed (F / R on the node) decides the written prompt; Re-roll writes a new one.
  • CLIP Text Encode (reads the prompt) - Reads the prompt through the text encoder.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. FLUX 3 distilled runs at CFG 1, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • Empty Flux 2 Latent (blank canvas) - The blank canvas the picture is painted on, at the size it receives.
  • KSampler (15 steps) - The render: 15 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple. Black Forest Labs' own workflow uses 16 steps. In our tests 8 steps gave nearly the same picture in about half the time; more than 16 steps made skin smoother and more waxy.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (saves the picture) - Saves each picture as PNG into ComfyUI/output/Flux 3 Klein Image to Prompt and shows it on the node.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Show Text Pixaroma (the prompt FLUX 3 gets) - Shows the prompt the AI wrote from your picture. Read it, copy it, or paste it into workflow 1 and edit it yourself.
  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the number of pictures and their size.

WhatTime
The AI looking and writing the promptabout 5 s
FLUX 3, 1024 x 1024about 3 s
One Run, start to endabout 8 s
A new picture seed, same promptabout 3 s

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models from disk (FLUX 3, its text encoder and the upsampler, about 18 GB together), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.
